assessment: The incumbent honored all designs and uses a reference-table check to catch errors, but seven covers required resewing and median time exceeded the target. Rework concentrated in large covers (5/8 versus 2/14 medium and 0/18 small), consistent with a size-dependent fitting problem; allowance, operator, direction and cloth effects remain unresolved. The concrete limitation is that both observed customer placement failures involved rounded corners absent from reference tables: passing the existing check does not establish customer fit. Small-cover times establish feasibility only for that subgroup. Estimated waste by weight does not establish compliance with the area limit.

openings.claim: The common cutting allowance may create systematic fit error as table size increases, making early size-specific calibration useful.
openings.delta: Sew and inspect initial examples before cutting the remaining stock; change allowances only if measured errors support doing so.
openings.prediction: Under matched cloth direction and operator, finished dimensional error increases with size; a calibrated allowance reduces that error and resewing on a subsequent large cover.
openings.probe: Record order, cut and finished dimensions and stage times on initial covers across sizes. Measure offcut length and width through the stipulated wash test. Trial any correction on the next comparable ordered cover; calculate layout waste by area before cutting. Include calibration labor when assessing batch time.
assumptions: A corrected layout fits purchased stock within 8% area waste.
Calibration and validation fit the three-week window and 350-unit budget.

openings.claim: Do rounded corners cause first-placement failures independently of inaccurate nominal length and width?
openings.delta: Test the specific geometry missing from the reference-table check before changing corner-pocket construction.
openings.prediction: If corner geometry matters independently, nominally matching rounded tables still fail when actual length and width match; if dimension error explains failures, placement follows dimensional mismatch instead.
openings.probe: Ask the six willing customers for actual dimensions and corner profiles, prioritizing nominal-only orders where possible. Observe first placement and compare tables with similar measured dimensions but different corners. Treat absent matched comparisons as inconclusive. Validate any resulting pocket revision for the ordered design, tool-free removal and five-cycle wash survival before adoption.
assumptions: Willing customers include informative geometry comparisons.
Measurements and installation observations are sufficiently consistent.
